item.title: Lions snap Packers' winning streak with Jake Bates' walk-off field goal
item.description: Jake Bates kicked a 22-yard field goal as time expired to give the host Detroit Lions a 20-17 victory over the Green Bay Packers on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jake Bates kicked a 22-yard field goal as time expired to give the host Detroit Lions a 20-17 victory over the Green Bay Packers on Sunday. Jared Goff passed for 303 yards and two touchdowns, both to Jameson Williams. Amon-Ra St. Brown caught nine passes for 153 yards and Williams hauled in five for 91 yards. Jahmyr Gibbs rushed for 116 yards on 29 carries for Detroit (4-2). Jordan Love passed for 274 yards, two touchdowns and one interception for Green Bay (4-3), which had its three-game winning streak snapped. Running back Josh Jacobs, activated off the NFL's exempt list, rushed for 36 yards and caught five passes for 55 yards and a touchdown in his season debut. The Lions drove 71 yards -- highlighted by an 18-yard catch by Sam LaPorta and a 15-yard run by Gibbs along with a key first-down pickup by Gibbs in the final minute -- to set up Bates' game-winning kick against their NFC North rivals. Detroit led 10-7 at halftime. Green Bay came up empty during the game's opening drive as Trey Smack missed a 26-yard field-goal attempt wide right. The Lions needed only six plays to drive 80 yards for their first score, a 16-yard scoring pass from Goff to Williams. The Packers answered with a 12-play, 74-yard drive that Love finished with a 14-yard strike to tight end Tucker Kraft. Bates' 40-yard field goal with 12:36 remaining in the half gave the Lions a 10-7 lead. Detroit drove 85 yards late in the half, but Gibbs lost a fumble on the Packers' 8-yard line. A Goff fumble on the second play from scrimmage in the third quarter allowed the Packers to take their only lead. Green Bay cashed in with a 25-yard pass from Love to Jacobs to gain a 14-10 advantage. The Lions regained the lead on their next possession as Goff capped an 80-yard march with a 10-yard pass over the middle to Williams. Lions coach Dan Campbell lost a gamble after his team drove inside the Packers' 10. Campbell went for it on fourth-and-5 from the 6, but Goff threw an incompletion intended for Williams. Smack's 43-yard field goal with 7:10 left tied the score at 17-17. The Lions gambled and lost again on their next drive. On fourth-and-1 from their own 24, Gibbs was tackled for a 2-yard loss by Keisean Nixon. The Detroit defense held, then D.J. Wonnum got a fingertip on Smack's 35-yard field-goal attempt to send it wide right with 3:21 to play. --Field Level Media

item.title: Trump says Canada tariff deal coming 'soon' at Michigan border rally
item.description: President Donald Trump at a Sunday political rally predicted a trade dispute with Canada would be resolved "soon," without providing specifics.
item.dc:creator: Valerie Volcovici
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump at a Sunday political rally predicted a trade dispute with Canada would be resolved "soon," without providing specifics. At an event in Port Huron, Michigan, to boost Republican candidates ahead of the November 3 midterms, Trump and other speakers reiterated his oft-expressed position that higher tariffs on Canadian goods are needed because Canada "has been ripping off" the US in trade. "I had to do it," Trump told the Michigan crowd. "We'll have that settled pretty soon. They're willing to give us anything at this moment." The office of Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Trump won in Michigan's border region that includes Port Huron in the 2024 presidential election with more than 66% of the vote, but the local economy has felt the impacts of the US-Canada tariff standoff, including the Detroit-based US auto industry. Republican Congressman Mike Rogers, who is running in a tight race against Democratic rival Abdul El-Sayed, has tried to distance himself from the president's tariff policy on the auto sector. Rogers on Sunday hailed Trump's tariffs for securing manufacturing investments for Michigan by Chevrolet and Detroit Diesel, but said "the automobile portion of these Canadian tariffs worries me a little bit." "There's some good and there's some things we have to work on," he told "Meet the Press."

item.title: China's tug-of-war with Australian miners lurks beneath iron ore calm
item.description: If China's iron ore market was to be judged by import volumes alone, the image would be one of gentle and steady growth.
item.dc:creator: Clyde Russell
item.content:encoded: If China's iron ore market was to be judged by import volumes alone, the image would be one of gentle and steady growth. But beneath the calm picture presented by imports of the main steel raw material is a tug-of-war between China, which buys about 75% of global seaborne supplies, and Australia's miners, which provide around two-thirds of China's needs. Beijing is attempting to gain more control of iron ore pricing, seeking to leverage its buying power to secure favourable terms. The problem is that Australian miners such as Rio Tinto (RIO.AX) (RIO.L) , BHP Group (BHP.AX) and Fortescue (FMG.AX) have considerable market power of their own as China has no alternative sources that supply the volume of required iron ore. China's imports of iron ore were 109.82 million metric tons in September, up 1.2% from August, while arrivals for the first nine months of 2026 were 954.97 million tons, an increase of 4.1%, according to customs data. October imports are likely to be similar to those for September with analysts DBX Commodities tracking seaborne arrivals of 105.7 million tons. China also buys small volumes overland from neighbouring countries. The modest gain in iron ore imports so far in 2026 comes despite weakness in the steel sector, which is suffering from weak profitability and declining production amid ongoing weakness in the key housing construction sector. Rather than being used to lift steel production, the gain in iron ore imports has largely flowed to rebuilding stockpiles. Port inventories monitored by consultants SteelHome were assessed at 152.23 million tons in the week to October 23, up 14% from 133.6 million in the same week in 2025. Lower prices in recent weeks have boosted import appetite, with Singapore Exchange contracts ending at $90.60 on October 23, down 19% from the $111.91 peak so far this year on May 11. CHINA MOVES The drift lower in iron ore prices also comes amid efforts by China's state-controlled buyer, China Mineral Resources Group (CMRG), which functions as an intermediary between iron ore miners and steel mills. In practical terms this has resulted in CMRG imposing a series of measures at various times against the Australian miners, in what are viewed by market participants as attempts to exert greater control over prices and supply contracts. CMRG reached a [USN:L1N4670LW TEXT:"supply deal"] with Rio Tinto, the world's largest iron ore miner, last week, according to people with knowledge of the matter, although details of the agreement were not immediately known. The deal came after CMRG instructed some steel mills in August to halt talks with Rio for September-loading cargoes. CMRG is still in dispute with Fortescue, with the company flagging on October 22 that if [USN:FWN467211 TEXT:"talks"] aren't concluded by the end of the year, operations may be affected. A similar dispute in which CMRG restricted purchases from BHP was resolved in April, and while terms weren't disclosed, it is believed the miner agreed to use several pricing indexes and accept small discounts. Overall, it would appear that CMRG is having some small success in extracting better terms from the Australian miners. However, China remains highly dependent on Australia for iron ore, and will remain so for years to come even as it seeks to diversify suppliers, with the ramp-up of the 120-million-tons-a-year Simandou project in Guinea being the primary example. It's also likely that iron ore prices will be driven mainly by the steel sector, and the decline in recent months tallies with lower steel production, which was down 2.9% in the first nine months of the year to 724.77 million tons. item.title: Mourinho gives Real Madrid the answers to Barcelona test in return to Clasico
item.description: Real Madrid recorded just a second victory in eight games against Barcelona on Sunday night, with the return of Jose Mourinho to the fixture haunting the reigning champions.
item.dc:creator: Ruairidh Barlow
item.content:encoded: Real Madrid recorded just a second victory in eight games against Barcelona on Sunday night, with the return of Jose Mourinho to the fixture haunting the reigning champions. In the first Clasico of Mourinho's first spell at Real Madrid, Barcelona ripped his side to shreds in a 5-0 win at Camp Nou. A [USN:L6N46B08P TEXT:"2-1 win"] in the first Clasico of his second spell suggests Mourinho's Real Madrid can challenge Barcelona's recent LaLiga dominance in his first season back in Spain. Although the chances were shared out evenly, with Barcelona racking up more shots on goal, more possession and more passes throughout the match, those statistics were not an honest reflection of the game. Real Madrid played as if they had the answers to the test Barcelona posed. "The lads played an extraordinary match," said Mourinho in his press conference afterwards. "Very organised, focused, and showing the courage to play the ball out from the back against an opponent that applied a lot of pressure." Time and again, Mourinho's side moved the ball with urgency and precision in their own half to escape Barcelona's pressing. Fede Valverde was praised for playing through injury by Mourinho, but above all he embodied the presence of mind to identify where the space was whenever the ball was turned over. The Uruguayan did so from the right-back position, despite stating in September 2025 that he was "not born to play as a full-back." Valverde later denied he had expressed any unwillingness to play in defence, but a number of Spanish outlets took this as a suggestion he was not pleased about doing so, and perhaps he was not on board with then-manager Xabi Alonso's style of management. For a third game in a row, the Real Madrid captain started at right-back and delivered a captain's performance. Valverde's impressive showing in his unfavoured position demonstrated Mourinho not only is finding tactical solutions to get the best out of his players, but is winning over the Real Madrid dressing room. Mourinho remarked that leaving Camp Nou just three points behind Barcelona "gives us peace of mind, and it's well deserved." The victory over Barcelona should help to boost morale and build unity within the Real Madrid squad. More importantly, Mourinho now has evidence his methods can help return Real Madrid to the summit of Spanish football. "If we win today but lose at El Sardinero, it counts for nothing, because Madrid isn't playing to win at the Camp Nou," Mourinho said. "They’re playing to win the championship" — a statement that now looks closer to reality after two defeats in September had sown early doubts about Mourinho's plans.

item.title: 76ers will rest Joel Embiid (foot) vs. Pistons
item.description: After recording his 11th career triple-double on Saturday versus the Milwaukee Bucks, Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid has been ruled out of Sunday's game against the Detroit Pistons to manage his workload. due to right foot plantar fasciitis management.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: After recording his 11th career triple-double on Saturday versus the Milwaukee Bucks, Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid has been ruled out of Sunday's game against the Detroit Pistons to manage his workload. due to right foot plantar fasciitis management. The oft-injured Embiid, who deals with plantar fasciitis in his right foot, told reporters after the 127-116 win over Milwaukee that he wanted to play against Detroit. "I actually want to play tomorrow, so can you guys put pressure on them," Embiid said. "... I want to play tomorrow, so start writing articles and put pressure on them so they'll let me play." But with LeBron James returning to the lineup versus the Pistons, the Sixers opted to stick with the plan to rest Embiid. James did not play (sciatica) against the Bucks. Embiid played 36 minutes on Saturday and amassed 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists as Philadelphia moved to 3-0. He leads the Sixers with 9.7 rebounds per game while ranking second in assists (5.7 apg) and third in scoring (21.7 ppg). James may have to play minutes at the center position as 76ers bigs Dominick Barlow (back), Jabari Walker (knee) and Tacko Fall (quad) are all on the shelf. Veteran Dean Wade, who scored seven points and added two rebounds and three steals in his Philadelphia debut on Saturday, and Adem Bona will also likely see time at center. --Field Level Media

item.title: Oil slips from near six-months highs despite supply concerns
item.description: Oil prices fell on Monday after surging to near six-month highs late last week, although ongoing attacks on Saudi Arabia kept supply concerns in focus.
item.dc:creator: Colleen Howe
item.content:encoded: Oil prices fell on Monday after surging to near six-month highs late last week, although ongoing attacks on Saudi Arabia kept supply concerns in focus. US crude futures were down $1.60, or 1.55%, at $101.67 per barrel by 0018 GMT. Brent crude futures were down $1.56 or 1.34% at $115.16. Prices had [USN:L1N46903W TEXT:"settled"] nearly $3 higher on Friday after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked energy supply concerns. Brent finished the week up 6% and WTI ended 2.3% higher. Attacks continued over the weekend with Houthis saying they had attacked the Saudi airport and oil facilities on Saturday. Saudi Arabia said on Sunday it had intercepted more missiles and drones. The top oil exporter [USN:L2N46A05D TEXT:"restarted"] partial operations at its main airport on Sunday after damage in a previous round of Houthi attacks even as the militant group vowed to keep targeting the facility.

item.title: Raptors F Kawhi Leonard (knee) out vs. Timbwerwolves
item.description: Toronto Raptors star forward Kawhi Leonard was scratched with left knee swelling about an hour before the team's Sunday night road game against the Minnesota Timberwolves.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Toronto Raptors star forward Kawhi Leonard was scratched with left knee swelling about an hour before the team's Sunday night road game against the Minnesota Timberwolves. Leonard has often experienced issues with both knees throughout his 15-year career. This is his first missed game since returning to the Raptors, whom he led to the 2019 NBA title. Leonard missed the 2021-22 season for the Los Angeles Clippers due to an ACL tear in his right knee. Leonard was acquired in the offseason from the Clippers. He is a seven-time All-Star and two-time NBA Finals MVP (once with Toronto, once with the San Antonio Spurs). The 35-year-old Leonard averaged 19.5 points, 7.5 rebounds and 3.5 steals as Toronto won its first two games of the season. However, he shot just 32.4% from the field and made 4 of 14 3-point attempts. --Field Level Media

item.title: Reactions to election victory of Serbia's Student List
item.description: Serbia's Aleksandar Vucic conceded defeat to a student-led protest movement in a historic election on Sunday that ends his long grip on power and heralds a new political era in the Balkan country.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Serbia's Aleksandar Vucic [USN:L6N46B017 TEXT:"conceded defeat"] to a student-led protest movement in a historic election on Sunday that ends his long grip on power and heralds a new political era in the Balkan country. Below are reactions to the students' victory: MILORAD DODIK, BOSNIAN SERB SEPARATIST AND PRO-RUSSIAN LEADER OF THE ALLIANCE OF INDEPENDENT SOCIAL DEMOCRATS "I congratulate the Student List on its victory. The citizens of Serbia and all political actors have once again demonstrated the democratic character of one of the oldest state-building nations in Europe." "Republika Srpska and Serbia continue forward together. The closest and in the best of relations. In cooperation and support on all issues — regional and international, at every forum and in every institution." "The voice of the people is the voice of God. The citizens of Republika Srpska and Serbia have spoken. We move forward — together," Dodik wrote on X. EUROPEAN COMMISSIONER FOR ENLARGEMENT, MARTA KOS "Serbia has raised its voice. After nearly two years of protests for democracy, the rule of law and the fight against corruption, the citizens of Serbia turned out to vote in historic numbers," Kos wrote in a statement to Slovenian correspondents from Brussels. URSULA VON DER LEYEN, HEAD OF THE EUROPEAN COMMISSION "Today, the people of Serbia turned out in record numbers to shape their country’s future. Congratulations to the Student List on its victory in the parliamentary elections. We stand ready to support reforms on the rule of law, media freedom, the fight against corruption and strong democratic institutions, and to work together to advance Serbia’s future in the European Union," von der Leyen wrote on X social media platform. SECRETARY-GENERAL OF THE COUNCIL OF EUROPE ALAIN BERSET "Congratulations to the Student List of Serbia on your electoral result. Serbian citizens have made their democratic choice. We welcome former President Vučić’s acceptance of the result and commitment to a peaceful democratic transition. Council of Europe stands ready to work with Serbia's democratically elected leadership to strengthen human rights, democracy and the rule of law. Your perseverance, energy and commitment to European principles and Serbia's future have brought you this far. You can count on our support," Berset wrote on X. MONTENEGRIN PRIME MINISTER MILOJKO SPAJIC "Today's events in Serbia are a vivid reminder that the will of the people and their right to freely decide their future are the foundation of every democratic change. The citizens of both countries deserve relations measured by concrete results of cooperation, not by the depth of diplomatic misunderstandings," Spajic wrote on X. HUNGARIAN PRIME MINISTER PETER MAGYAR "I have just spoken by phone with the leaders of the Students' List, who won the elections in Serbia, to congratulate them on their victory. I assured them of Hungary’s support. I was delighted to hear how much strength our victory in April had given them during this difficult struggle," Magyar wrote on X.

item.title: Why China’s stimulus keeps missing the mark
item.description: China's economy has split in two: high-tech exports are surging, while domestic consumption and job creation are stalling. Now that major trading partners are seeking to put up more barriers, Beijing may need to rethink its cautious approach to direct household stimulus.
item.dc:creator: Manishi Raychaudhuri
item.content:encoded: China's economy has split in two: high-tech exports are surging, while domestic consumption and job creation are stalling. Now that major trading partners are seeking to put up more barriers, Beijing may need to rethink its cautious approach to direct household stimulus. China's K-shaped economy was clearly illustrated by its third-quarter GDP figures. Exceptional export growth, driven by global AI spending and clean energy investment, helped GDP growth hit 4.5% year-on-year. While retail sales rose slightly, the increase came from a low base, and the multi-year housing slump continued to weigh on the domestic economy. The housing slump partly explains the consumption woes. With residential property accounting for about 70% of Chinese household assets on average, dwindling home prices since 2021 have eroded household wealth and constrained consumption. Meanwhile, increasing job insecurity appears to be driving up precautionary savings. The official urban unemployment rate has held around 5% over the past three years, but youth unemployment has hovered between 14% and 19%, underscoring the obstacles to creating new jobs. A 2024 survey by the People’s Bank of China attributed the country’s rising savings rate to the weak job market. DIVERGENT BY DESIGN This divergent growth pattern reflects Beijing's policy choices. Technological self-sufficiency has long been China's stated long-term strategic goal. China's “New Quality Productive Forces” growth model, articulated in late 2023 , called for generous investment in digitalization, networking, biotechnology and AI. In March, the [USN:L8N3ZR09Y TEXT:"15th Five-Year Plan"] reinforced this model, elevating six emerging industries – AI and robotics, semiconductors, advanced mobile communications, quantum technologies, biotechnology and drones and air taxis – as pillars of future growth. There may be merits to this strategy given the tech arms race with the US, but it appears to come at the expense of domestic consumption, as it generates negative wealth effects, limits the resources available for social safety nets and reduces support for labor-intensive industries. For example, since 2020, Beijing has [USN:L6N45703P TEXT:"shifted policy"] to divert capital away from real estate and toward advanced manufacturing and green energy. In this period, outstanding bank loans to the property sector have flattened, while those to manufacturing and green technology have grown at annual rates of 10-15% and 20-40%, respectively. This, in turn, has inhibited the recovery in the property sector, which has weighed on domestic consumption. While generous investments in advanced manufacturing and green technology may boost GDP growth, they have not alleviated the country's unemployment problem. As the International Monetary Fund (IMF) [USN:L1N3LX0C0 TEXT:"has warned"], the shift toward sectors like electric vehicles (EVs) reshapes employment toward capital-intensive, highly automated production rather than broad job creation. Moreover, [USN:L4N2P31JT TEXT:"regulatory crackdowns"] have negatively impacted white-collar work: research on China's private education ban shows it wiped out 3 million jobs alone, alongside massive layoffs at [USN:L5N2VH0RL TEXT:"internet platforms"] and developers. Even though Beijing’s focus on advanced manufacturing, AI, clean energy and other industries of the future makes strategic sense on the global stage – and may be the envy of the US and the European Union – at home, these priorities have left Chinese consumers facing a host of economic headwinds. NARROWING OPTIONS The combination of breathtaking expansion in manufacturing capacity and weak domestic demand has led to overcapacity in many sectors, much of which has been exported – a [USN:L6N45Z06C TEXT:"charge frequently levelled"] by the US and the EU. This overcapacity has driven a destructive race for domestic market share, crushing prices and margins across EVs, solar panels, batteries and e-commerce. So far, Beijing's plans to combat this "involution" have met with limited success. Meanwhile, major trading partners, including [USN:S8N42Q0FC TEXT:"the EU"], are beginning to erect trade barriers, narrowing the scope for export-led growth. This highlights the risks China could face if it fails to revive household consumption. China has periodically attempted to boost domestic demand. A coordinated [USN:L1N3L6043 TEXT:"monetary"] and [USN:L4N3LN0KU TEXT:"fiscal"] package in September 2024 included sharp cuts to banks' reserve requirement ratios and benchmark policy rates, as well as relaxed home-purchase restrictions. The central government also embarked on local-government debt resolution and support for low-income households. In contrast, a new set of measures announced [USN:P8N44P093 TEXT:"last month"] was much less ambitious, focusing on capital injections into state-owned banks and insurance companies as well as consumer credit subsidies. Chinese policymakers have also been reluctant to commit to concrete consumption targets. Several government advisers [USN:L4N3T10FN TEXT:"recommended"] that the upcoming 15th Five-Year Plan include a target to raise household consumption from 40% of GDP to 50% over the next two five-year cycles, but that recommendation went unheeded. The lighter fiscal touch is not surprising given growing debt constraints. China's total government debt, including central, local and off-balance-sheet government financing vehicles, has risen from 80% of GDP in 2019 to 127% in 2025, according to the IMF. Additionally, rebalancing the economy would require more than fiscal and monetary support. The IMF has suggested reallocating public resources from production to households, enhancing social safety nets for healthcare, unemployment and pensions, and relaxing the household registration system, or hukou, to grant urban status to 200 million rural migrant workers. But such recommendations have received a lukewarm response. While some officials in Beijing have indicated that the country should rebalance away from exports and toward consumption, doing so would likely mean slower growth in the short term and could require adjustments that would be painful to certain segments of the economy. Ultimately, China's economic rebalancing faces a deep structural impasse. Whether it can overcome it may be the key question for the global economy in the next decade. item.title: Belgrade in rapture as Serbian students topple Vucic in historic election
item.description: Trams and traffic halted by crowds. Tens of thousands of people choking the city's main boulevards; the air thick with smoke; a man on a car waving a flare.
item.dc:creator: Edward Mcallister, Kirsten Donovan, Aleksandar Vasovic
item.content:encoded: Trams and traffic halted by crowds. Tens of thousands of people choking the city's main boulevards; the air thick with smoke; a man on a car waving a flare. Familiar-sounding scenes after a month of sometimes violent protests across European cities as students take to the streets calling for better education standards and better prospects. Except, on Sunday night in Serbia's capital Belgrade, students were not protesting but celebrating an election victory after long-time ruler Aleksandar Vucic [USN:L6N46B017 TEXT:"conceded defeat"] to a student-backed list of candidates in parliamentary elections. It was the culmination of a two-year, [USN:L8N4650K6 TEXT:"peaceful protest movement"] that called for Vucic to step down and an end to what they said is rampant corruption in the Balkan country - a charge Vucic denies. The students' win marks a profound political shift in the country of some 6 million people and shows what power younger generation have when they are able to harness widespread discontent. "That is the best thing that happened in my life. We will now breathe freely," said Milica, a law student. Vucic had ruled as prime minister or president since 2014, and oversaw a period of strong economic growth, but he faced growing opposition from student-led protests after the collapse of a railway station awning killed 16 people in November 2024. Tomorrow, the disparate group of 250 student-backed candidates will have to turn towards ruling, but Sunday evening was a time to party. At their headquarters, the unknown candidates, many of them lawyers, professors, actors or farmers, hugged and cheered in near disbelief at what they had achieved. "The people have won! The people defeated a dictator! The people will lead Serbia!" said Nebojsa Cosic while waving a flag on the street.

item.title: Real Madrid derrota 2-1 al Barcelona en el Camp Nou con doblete de Mbappé y se acerca
item.description: El Real Madrid se convirtió el domingo en el primer equipo en vencer al Barcelona en LaLiga esta temporada al vencer 2-1 al campeón defensor en el Camp Nou con un doblete de Kylian Mbappé.
item.dc:creator: Ruairidh Barlow
item.content:encoded: El Real Madrid se convirtió el domingo en el primer equipo en vencer al Barcelona en LaLiga esta temporada al vencer 2-1 al campeón defensor en el Camp Nou con un doblete de Kylian Mbappé. El undécimo gol de Mbappé en 10 partidos de LaLiga le dio la victoria al DT José Mourinho en su regreso al Clásico 13 años después de que terminara su primera etapa en el Real Madrid. Con el triunfo, los blancos redujeron la diferencia con el Barcelona a solo tres puntos. En una primera parte muy igualada, ambos equipos crearon una serie de ocasiones de gol, pero las incursiones ofensivas del Madrid tuvieron mucha más determinación. La frustración de Hansi Flick en la banda sirvió como prueba de que el plan de juego de Mourinho estaba funcionando mejor que el suyo. En el minuto 41, Yan Diomande centró desde la izquierda y el despeje suave de Gerard Martin rebotó en Mbappé, que salía a su encuentro, y el balón acabó en el fondo de la red. El Barcelona tuvo la oportunidad de empatar antes del descanso tras un rebote, pero Lamine Yamal no pudo convertir desde cerca. El Barca igualó en el minuto 61, cuando un pase de Pedri encontró a Raphinha con espacio en el área. El brasileño remató cruzado para poner el 1-1. La rápida circulación del balón del Madrid en su propio campo siguió dejando al descubierto la defensa del Barcelona en los primeros compases de la segunda parte, pero tras el gol, a los visitantes les resultó cada vez más difícil escapar de la presión del conjunto culé. Pese a todo, la defensa del Madrid logró sostenerse, y el equipo de Mourinho seguía generando peligro en ataque. Esa convicción defensiva tuvo su recompensa a tres minutos del final. Un mal control de Gabriel Jesus propició un contraataque del Madrid. Eduardo Camavinga logró colarse entre la defensa antes de pasarle el balón a Mbappé, quien solo tuvo que empujarlo a la red vacía. El triunfo fue lo suficientemente convincente como para sugerir que el Madrid supondrá un serio desafío al título para el equipo catalán tras dos temporadas decepcionantes. "Ha sido un gran partido, que seguramente todo el mundo que ama el fútbol se ha parado para ver, con dos equipos que jugaron a ganar y en nuestro caso (...) los chicos han hecho un partido extraordinario, muy organizados, concentrados, con coraje para salir jugando desde atrás con un adversario que presiona mucho", dijo Mourinho tras el encuentro. El Barcelona se mantiene líder de LaLiga con 27 puntos en 10 partidos, uno más que el Atlético de Madrid, que aparece segundo. El Real Madrid, tercero, suma 24 unidades.

item.title: Anthropic's Claude accessed Georgia state vote count data behind paywall
item.description: AI model Claude bypassed a paywall and accessed publicly available US state of Georgia aggregate voter counts without human authorization, Anthropic said in a statement on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: AI model Claude bypassed a paywall and accessed publicly available US state of Georgia aggregate voter counts without human authorization, Anthropic said in a statement on Sunday. "Claude didn't access the state's voter registration system or change or pull any voting records," Anthropic said, adding that it has since taken steps to block these kinds of actions. Anthropic said in a blog post earlier this month it found examples of Claude "working around a restriction to reach data that was gated by a token or a fee" and some of these cases involved websites run by US government agencies at the federal, state, and local levels. The secretary of state's office in Georgia did not respond to a Reuters request for comment outside regular business hours. Axios first reported the unauthorized action by Claude.

item.content:encoded: O Real Madrid tornou-se neste domingo a primeira equipe a derrotar o Barcelona na atual temporada da LaLiga, ao vencer o clássico por 2 a 1 no Camp Nou, com dois gols de Kylian Mbappé. O atacante francês abriu o placar aos 41 minutos do primeiro tempo ao desviar para o gol uma tentativa de corte de Gerard Martín. O Barcelona empatou aos 16 minutos da etapa final. Após uma cobrança rápida de escanteio, Pedri encontrou Raphinha livre na área, e o brasileiro bateu no canto, sem chances para o goleiro Andriy Lunin. Quando a partida parecia caminhar para o empate, Eduardo Camavinga avançou pela esquerda e cruzou para Mbappé marcar o gol da vitória aos 42 minutos do segundo tempo. Apesar da derrota, o Barcelona segue na liderança da LaLiga, com 27 pontos em 10 jogos, um a mais que o vice-líder Atlético de Madrid. O Real Madrid ocupa a terceira colocação, com 24 pontos. item.title: UK commits to further £432 million to end rough sleeping
item.description: Britain's government said on Sunday it would almost double its funding for efforts to end rough sleeping and give homeless people a way to get off the streets in the winter months.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Britain's government said on Sunday it would almost double its funding for efforts to end rough sleeping and give homeless people a way to get off the streets in the winter months. Prime Minister Andy Burnham and finance minister John Healey said they would commit a further £432 million ($577.7 million) of funding for the plan, which offers accommodation and support, to run until the scheduled end of parliament in 2029. Burnham said on his first day in Downing Street in July that he wanted to end rough sleeping. He was due to meeting local leaders, businesses and charities on Monday to discuss the plan. Healey is scheduled to announce his first budget plan on Wednesday. ($1 = 0.7478 pounds)

item.title: Leafs riding 'great' vibes while Flames try to finish perfect homestand
item.description: The Calgary Flames and visiting Toronto Maple Leafs will strive to continue their win streaks in the face of key injury absences when they meet on Monday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Calgary Flames and visiting Toronto Maple Leafs will strive to continue their win streaks in the face of key injury absences when they meet on Monday night. The Maple Leafs will wrap up the Alberta section of their road trip coming off the high point of their season so far. Toronto scored four third-period goals in a 7-2 battering of Edmonton on Saturday to extend its winning streak to four games, its first of that length since January. "The vibes are great," said goaltender Anthony Stolarz, who made 30 saves on the night. "We got a great group, an influx of kids that have a lot of energy, and they're really bringing out the best in everyone. It's an exciting time to be a Maple Leaf." The ongoing absence of second-line center John Tavares (lower-body injury) has afforded head coach Jim Hiller the opportunity to prove that the Maple Leafs' forward corps offers more than the one-two punch of years past. Thirteen different players recorded a point on Saturday, and every member of the fourth line -- Brandon Duhaime, Teddy Blueger and Zack MacEwen -- nabbed their first goal in blue and white over the last two games. As a team, Toronto has scored 18 goals over the last three. "That to me says something about your team. That says you've got depth. That says it's not just (Auston) Matthews. It's not just (William) Nylander. It's not just Tavares. It's going through the lineup, and that gives you a chance to win every night," Hiller said. Toronto conceded its first power-play goal on the road against the Oilers, though they still lead the NHL in penalty kill percentage (95.2%) and special-teams efficiency (125.4%). After losing six of their first seven games, the Flames will have a chance to extend their own winning streak to four as they wrap up their four-game homestand. Devin Cooley made 28 saves as Calgary thumped the Detroit Red Wings 4-1 Saturday. "We've just been stacking wins and stacking good play the last couple games here," said Joel Farabee, who had three points on the night. "We just have a little bit of confidence and a little bit of swagger right now that maybe we didn't have the first five or six games of the season. We're just finding how we have to play to win and just trying not to do too much and playing simple." The Flames have managed to reverse their fortunes with something of a depleted offense. Jonathan Huberdeau (hip) remains sidelined for the foreseeable future while captain Mikael Backlund (upper-body injury) has missed the last two outings. Lacking genuine star power at the top of their lineup, Calgary will continue to count on a distributed workload and a high-functioning power play, which is 6-for-12 over its last four games. Nine of the team's 12 forwards logged at least twelve minutes at even strength against Detroit. "When the power play is scoring and things are going their way, they start feeling really good about playing on the ice and they know they can be difference-makers and that's the phase they're in right now," said head coach Ryan Huska. Toronto will likely continue to rotate players in and out of their defensive pairings amid the injury absences of Chris Tanev, Nick Blankenburg and Marshall Rifai. The Maple Leafs have won the last eight encounters between the two teams. --Field Level Media

item.title: New-look Heat search for first win as Mavericks visit
item.description: With three losses to open the season, the Miami Heat are still looking for the first win of the Giannis Antetokounmpo Era.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: With three losses to open the season, the Miami Heat are still looking for the first win of the Giannis Antetokounmpo Era. The Heat get another shot at that elusive victory on Monday night when they play host to the Dallas Mavericks. Antetokounmpo averaged 35.5 points in his first two games in a Heat uniform, but he was held to 14 on Saturday in a 115-110 loss at Charlotte. He played just 25 minutes before fouling out with 1:57 remaining. A 10-time All-Star, two-time NBA MVP and one-time league champion, Antetokounmpo was the prize in the huge offseason trade with the Milwaukee Bucks. But the question then -- and now -- was whether Miami gave up too much to get him. Specifically, do the Heat have enough shooters to put around him? Bam Adebayo, Miami's other established star, is off to a slow start as he averages 13.0 points and 7.0 rebounds per game. Point guard Davion Mitchell has stepped up, averaging 17.0 points on 46.7% 3-point shooting. Both numbers would easily be career highs for Mitchell, a player known more for tight defense. Aside from those three players, nobody on the Heat averages more than 10.3 points. Andrew Wiggins (18.2% on 3-point attempts) and Tim Hardaway Jr. (17.6% from deep) are off to poor shooting starts that are similar to Adebayo (23.1%) and Antetokounmpo (16.7%). Miami coach Erik Spoelstra knows it's early, though, and said this is all part of this version of the Heat learning to handle adversity. "We're all on the same page when shots are going down," Spoelstra said after the loss to Charlotte. "But when the game goes the other way, we really introduce ourselves to each other and collectively build a resolve." Meanwhile, the Mavericks are coming off a 122-106 home loss to San Antonio on Saturday. Dallas played without reigning Rookie of the Year Cooper Flagg, who injured his left shoulder in a 121-105 win over Indiana on Friday and will be re-evaluated this week. Nine-time All-Star Kyrie Irving, coming off knee surgery, also sat against San Antonio but is expected to be ready to face the Heat. Without that duo on Saturday, Dallas was led by rookie reserve Sergio de Larrea, the No. 25 pick in this year's draft (by the Los Angeles Lakers). A native of Spain, de Larrea is a skilled combo guard listed at 6-foot-5 and 175 pounds. At age 20, he offers Dallas hope that he could develop into a star. He produced 21 points, five rebounds and four assists in 33 minutes against the Spurs after going scoreless in eight minutes during the Mavs' first two games. "Today it was me, but other days it will be other guys," said de Larrea. "I'm waiting every day for this moment. I'm just trying to be prepared, but I have a lot to improve." Irving, if he's ready, will try to improve on his 19.5 scoring average. Flagg leads the team with 23.0 points per game. --Field Level Media

item.title: Australia's NEXTDC CEO to forgo fiscal 2027 bonuses after forecast cut, project delay
item.description: NEXTDC CEO Craig Scroggie will give up his fiscal 2027 bonus opportunities, the Australian data centre operator said on Monday, after it slashed its revenue forecast and paused future developments last week.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: NEXTDC (NXT.AX) CEO Craig Scroggie will give up his fiscal 2027 bonus opportunities, the Australian data centre operator said on Monday, after it slashed its revenue forecast and paused future developments [USN:L4N4661TS TEXT:"last week"]. Here are some details: The company said the board has withdrawn the resolution proposing an approval of grant of performance rights and restricted rights to the CEO under the fiscal 2027 long term incentive plan. Current Chairman Douglas Flynn has reaffirmed his intention to retire from the board once a new chairman is in place, after a short handover period. The board expects to appoint two new non-executive directors in the first calendar quarter of 2027, NEXTDC added. The company said the board has also withdrawn the resolution seeking shareholder approval to increase the maximum aggregate annual remuneration of non-executive directors by A$300,000 ($210,660), with the incumbent non-executive directors also agreeing to an immediate voluntary 10% reduction in their current fees. Last week, NEXTDC said delays to electricity network upgrades at one of its major Melbourne projects would mean about A$140 million worth of contracted customer revenue this financial year would be deferred. The firm is set to hold its annual general meeting on November 20. ($1 = 1.4241 Australian dollars)

item.title: Wizards, Hornets out to capitalize on early-season momentum
item.description: The Washington Wizards and host Charlotte Hornets have plenty of positives to build on heading into their meeting Monday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Washington Wizards and host Charlotte Hornets have plenty of positives to build on heading into their meeting Monday night. Both teams won Saturday, providing encouraging signs early in the season. Still, nothing has come easily for the Hornets in their first two home games. They lost by 47 points to Atlanta before watching a 23-point lead evaporate against Miami, then recovering to win 115-110. Brandon Miller led the way with 34 points against the Heat, matching the third-highest total of his four-year career. "Every game is not going to be perfect," Miller said. "Our mindset, other teams are going to go on runs and it's how we respond to it." The Wizards won their road opener 124-120 at Chicago on Saturday, with Trae Young scoring 25 points. Young will be a familiar opponent for Charlotte after making numerous appearances against the Hornets with the Atlanta Hawks. He has led Washington in scoring in each of the past two games after Anthony Davis poured in 34 points in the opener. "We were able to establish physicality," Wizards coach Brian Keefe said. "We stayed with it, and that was the part that was really great." Washington also likes what it has seen from Kyshawn George, particularly his ability to defend bigger players, according to Keefe. "That's why this team is so fun to coach because they want to put the time in," Keefe said. "Kyshawn is right at the top." No. 1 overall pick AJ Dybantsa has yet to make his Wizards debut while dealing with a left ankle injury. He will miss his fourth consecutive game Monday. Washington has shown depth, however, with 10 players seeing action against Chicago. In Saturday's victory, the Hornets benefited from late-game contributions by veteran newcomers Naz Reid and Grayson Allen. It was Charlotte's first home win of the season. "I think they're a big piece of what we're building here," Miller said. "Those are guys who have obviously been to the playoffs and been to places we want to be." Reid said he recognized how quickly the home crowd had embraced his play. Charlotte's veteran core will look to make an impact in close games as the season progresses. "We've been in enough of those situations in our past," Reid said. "Knowing how to keep our composure. ... Those are fun, especially with the home crowd." Hornets coach Charles Lee said the early-season games provide valuable opportunities to evaluate the team, adding that veteran Dennis Schroder has shown he can be a defensive presence. "Just really impressed with the whole group," Lee said. Miller has shot 29.7% from the field through three games after shooting nearly 43% for his career. "That's why you never overreact to shooting numbers or shooting slumps," Lee said. "That guy has a body of work that is just very impressive." The Hornets played their first three games without Kon Knueppel (hamstring), Coby White (calf) and Grant Williams (hamstring). Knueppel resumed individual on-court activity nearly a week ago, but no target date has been set for his return. Charlotte swept the four-game season series in 2025-26 after Washington won the previous five matchups. --Field Level Media

item.title: Real Madrid defeat Barcelona at Camp Nou to halve gap to LaLiga leaders
item.description: Real Madrid became the first side to beat Barcelona in LaLiga this season, defeating the league leaders 2-1 at Camp Nou with a brace from Kylian Mbappe.
item.dc:creator: Ruairidh Barlow
item.content:encoded: Real Madrid became the first side to beat Barcelona in LaLiga this season, defeating the league leaders 2-1 at Camp Nou with a brace from Kylian Mbappe. Mbappe's 11th goal in 10 LaLiga matches secured victory for Jose Mourinho in his return to El Clasico 13 years after his first spell at Real Madrid ended. Real halved the gap to league leaders Barcelona to three points. Both sides created a series of half-chances early on, but Real's forays forward came with far more resolve. Barca manager Hansi Flick's frustration on the touchline served as evidence that Mourinho's game plan was functioning better than his own. In the 41st minute, Yan Diomande crossed from the left and Gerard Martin's soft clearance hit the onrushing Mbappe, bouncing off him and into the net. Barcelona had the chance to level before the break after a fortunate ricochet, but Lamine Yamal couldn't convert from close range. It was a set piece that undid Real in the 61st minute, with Pedri's reverse pass finding Raphinha in space in the box and the Brazilian finishing into the corner. Real's swift movement of the ball in their own half continued to expose the Barcelona backline in the early stages of the second half. However, following the goal, the visitors found it increasingly hard to escape Barcelona's pressing. Barcelona's attacks were now finishing with last-ditch blocks from the Real defence, even if Mourinho's side continued to carry a threat going forward. That defensive conviction was rewarded with three minutes remaining. A loose touch from Barcelona substitute Gabriel Jesus set Real on the counter-attack, and substitute Eduardo Camavinga had enough pace to get in behind the defence, before squaring the ball for Mbappe to tap into the empty net. Barcelona remain top of the standings with 27 points from 10 games, one ahead of Atletico Madrid in second place. Third-place Real Madrid are on 24 points. Earlier Athletic Club beat Getafe 4-0 and Real Sociedad won 2-1 against Levante. Real Betis remain fourth after drawing 0-0 with Celta Vigo.

item.title: Lars Eller scores first goal as Panther in narrow win over Blackhawks
item.description: Lars Eller tallied the go-ahead goal with 2:23 remaining in the third period and Sandis Vilmanis and Matthew Tkachuk also scored to lift the visiting Florida Panthers to a 3-2 victory against the Chicago Blackhawks on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Lars Eller tallied the go-ahead goal with 2:23 remaining in the third period and Sandis Vilmanis and Matthew Tkachuk also scored to lift the visiting Florida Panthers to a 3-2 victory against the Chicago Blackhawks on Sunday. Panthers goaltender Akira Schmid stopped 20 shots as Florida snapped a two-game losing streak. Schmid turned aside Cole Smith on a breakaway with 5:45 to keep the game tied at 2. Eller netted his first goal of the season at 17:37 of the third period as the Panthers caught the Blackhawks in a line change. Eller took a long pass from Aaron Ekblad just inside the blue line, weaved down the right side and ripped a wrist shot from the circle past Chicago goaltender Spencer Knight. For the 37-old-year Eller, it was also his first goal as a member of the Florida Panthers. He started his NHL career with the St. Louis Blues in the 2009-10 season and has played for the Montreal Canadiens (2010-16), Washington Capitals (2016-23, 2024-25), Colorado Avalanche (2023), Pittsburgh Penguins (2023-25) and Ottawa Senators (2025-26). Special-teams struggles hurt the Blackhawks, who went 0-for-7 on the power play while also failing to capitalize on other chances at even strength. Knight made 29 saves. Chicago managed just six shots in the first period, but one of the club's early attempts provided a 1-0 lead. Ryan Greene tracked a puck that bounced at the top of the crease and into the air and batted it past Schmid and into the net. Andrew Mangiapane earned the primary assist in his return to the lineup; the forward had been out after suffering a lower-body injury in the club's season opener on Sept. 29. Florida tied the game just over four minutes later, as Vilmanis backhanded a loose puck past Knight after the backstop made a save on Sam Reinhart. The Panthers took a 2-1 lead on Matthew Tkachuk's power-play goal at 14:21. Tkachuk deflected Seth Jones' shot from the point just five seconds into the man advantage. Chicago netted the equalizer at 11:15 of the second period when Roman Kantserov took a Patrick Kane feed from behind the net and scored on a wrist shot from the right circle. Florida limited Chicago to one shot on goal during a four-minute power-play early in the second period after Carter Verhaeghe was whistled for a high-sticking double-minor against the Blackhawks' Wyatt Kaiser. Verhaeghe sent a wrist shot off the crossbar on a breakaway moments after springing from the penalty box. The Blackhawks fell to 2-4-0 on a seven-game homestand that is set to conclude with Tuesday's visit from the Los Angeles Kings. --Field Level Media

item.title: North Korea tells UN South fabricated landmine incident, KCNA says
item.description: North Korea said it had written to the UN Security Council, accusing South Korea of fabricating a September landmine incident and endangering troops working to fortify the border, state media KCNA reported on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: North Korea said it had written to the UN Security Council, accusing South Korea of fabricating a September landmine incident and endangering troops working to fortify the border, state media KCNA reported on Monday. On Sunday, North Korea's UN representative said in a letter Seoul was using the landmine incident to depict Pyongyang's border construction as a military incursion, and warned violations of its sovereignty could trigger self-defence, according to KCNA. It concerns explosions on September 21 in the Demilitarised Zone between the two Koreas that seriously hurt two South Korean soldiers. Seoul subsequently said mines North Korea planted south of the Military Demarcation Line that runs through the DMZ caused the blasts. The UN Command said a North Korean mine across the line violated the armistice. Pyongyang has denied responsibility. North Korea's letter also accused South Korea of opening fire on North Korean personnel, calling it a violation of the UN Charter, which bars the threat or use of force against another state's territorial integrity. Seoul has said it gives warning broadcasts and fires warning shots to make North Korean soldiers return north when they cross the MDL. North Korean troops have been building tactical roads and fences and laying mines near the MDL in recent years. Last Friday, South Korea's defence ministry again [USN:L1N46905T TEXT:"proposed"] military talks with North Korea to reduce the risk of accidental clashes.

item.title: Bulls searching for shooting aim entering clash vs. Celtics
item.description: The Chicago Bulls are still looking for ways to improve their 3-point shooting, an issue that has carried over from the offseason into the early stages of the season.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Chicago Bulls are still looking for ways to improve their 3-point shooting, an issue that has carried over from the offseason into the early stages of the season. Entering Monday night's road game against the Boston Celtics, the Bulls ranked 17th among the 30 NBA teams in 3-point percentage during the 2025-26 regular season but sit last in the league through three games this season at 22.6%. Chicago is averaging 9.3 made 3-pointers on 41.3 attempts per game. "I want them to shoot the ball," Chicago coach Tiago Splitter said following Saturday's 124-120 loss to Washington. "They can shoot. Part of their development is you are open, you got to shoot it. You practice every day; you have to take them in the game. Sometimes it's the shot the other team is giving to you. It's a team thing, not just one player. Everybody's got to be better. We don't have a 7-3 guy that's going to clean up the whole thing. So it's got to be a team effort and awareness." The Bulls went 12-for-43 from 3-point range against the Wizards. Caleb Wilson, the fourth pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, scored a game-high 30 points but went 1-for-9 from beyond the arc. Jalen Smith and Matas Buzelis each went 2-for-7. "We all knew coming into season (3-point shooting was) one of things we've got to get better and develop," Splitter said. "Caleb one of nine, Matas two of seven - those are the guys who are going to take shots. They are going to get better. But shoot (28) percent, you've really got to win the possession game to win when you are not shooting the ball well." Chicago has struggled defensively as well, allowing 128.0 points per game. Only Milwaukee (129.0) has allowed more. Boston bounced back from a season-opening 121-113 loss at Detroit by beating New York 107-103 at home Friday night. Jayson Tatum scored a game-high 36 points and grabbed nine rebounds in the win. The Celtics also received strong performances from center Neemias Queta and guard/forward Jordan Walsh. Queta started at center for Boston last season but now comes off the bench after the Celtics acquired Mitchell Robinson in the offseason. Queta had 15 points, six rebounds and three blocked shots in 22 minutes against the Knicks. Walsh, known primarily for his defense, has started both of Boston's games. He helped limit New York's Jalen Brunson to 19 points on 7-of-17 shooting. Walsh, who signed a three-year, $15 million extension last summer, was assigned to guard Cade Cunningham in Boston's opener. "I thought he was special (against New York)," Boston's Paul George said. "He set the tone. Jalen is a handful, and for a young guy he can be a lot. Jordan took the challenge. He did a great job of navigating being physical and not being overly physical. He gave him some good looks defensively to frustrate him and get him out of rhythm."
